cases.query: How are IOC and PV information managed in SHINE?

response.answer:
The lifecycle runs from generation to storage to use: scripting codes embedded in the IOC startup script automatically push the server's address, the IOC installation path and all records maintained by the IOC to the application as soon as the IOC starts up, and these are then stored in the database. A MySQL-backed application runs periodically and takes data from run-time databases via Channel Access and pvAccess. The database is a general storage container for the properties and real-time values of servers, IOCs, EPICS records and PVs. With this necessary information, all active IOCs and PVs can be accessed, and a web application renders servers, IOCs and PVs data in MySQL on the web to give an overall running status of the control system. [1][2]

IOC information is registered and collected automatically: scripting codes embedded in the IOC startup script push the server's address, the IOC installation path and all records maintained by the IOC to the application as soon as the IOC starts up. The program then parses the text file for the installation path, IP address, epics ca server port, epics ca repeater port and lists of the record for an IOC. The IOC related information is stored to the ioc table, while the record related information is inserted into the record table. [1][3]

PV information is collected two ways: the import service imports initial information such as record types, field name lists and field types into the relational database from a spreadsheet, and PV service fetches PVs from EPICS run-time databases via Channel Access and pvAccess while also retrieving server running information such as available free memory and CPU load, then saves all the data into the database. The values of fields, the so-called PVs, are stored in the field_value table. [2][4]

The database is a general storage container for the properties and real-time values of servers, IOCs, EPICS records and PVs. The values of fields, the so-called PVs, are stored in the field_value table. [2][4]

A web application renders servers, IOCs and PVs data in MySQL on the web to give an overall running status of the control system. The IOC panel displays not only the running information of the IOC but also all the records included in the IOC, and the record panel displays all the fields' information. [1][5]

cases.query: How are the functional layers of the SHINE control system separated?

response.answer:
The SHINE control system is divided into four layers to ensure performance and scalability: the operator interface layer, the middle layer, the device control layer and the data acquisition layer. [1]

The operator interface layer provides a GUI, CLI and high-level API to operators, engineers and physicists. [1]

The device control layer handles facility-wide input and output device control, such as magnet power supply, vacuum gauge and stepper motor control, and also hosts the machine protection and timing system. [2]

The data acquisition layer is designed for high-speed image and stream data acquisition, processing and storage. [2]

cases.query: How do PLCs and soft IOCs divide control and PV acquisition in the SHINE cryogenic system?

response.answer:
PLCs carry most of the control logic and the PID cycle; the low-level control logic and loops for the different operational modes are written in LADDER or SCL and reside in the PLC. [1][2]

Loops running on the PLCs must work continuously and cannot tolerate even momentary interruptions, whereas a short interruption can be tolerated in the IOC; therefore non-critical controls such as cryostat operational modes are implemented in the IOC with State Notation Language (SNL), which allows IOC reboot for maintenance and modification while the PLC keeps the values of all inputs and outputs when IOC–PLC communication is broken for a while. [2]

The EPICS PID record is used in the IOC, allowing easy adjustment of loop constants and loop parameters and providing the digital enabling interface for software protection of the cryogenic system. [2]

At the device level, components such as sensors, actuators and measurement devices are interfaced to local PLCs with touch panel through different types of signal transition. [1]

Soft IOCs running the EPICS runtime database accomplish signal collection from the PLC and convert the signals to Process Variables (PV) under the EPICS Channel Access (CA) protocol. [1]

Communication between PLCs and IOCs is implemented by the S7nodave EPICS device support driver resident on the IOC, which just specifies the memory address in the PLC and uses the ISO-TCP protocol supported by most S7 PLCs to exchange data. [3]
